title: What are you doing this week?
content_html:
I appreciate it and was actually thinking of starting to blog about it (cooklog?!). Haven’t tried bread yet but successfully made homemade pasta this weekend that was a hit. She’s not the first in her family to be diagnosed, she’s in fact the second-last… only her brother remains and he’s going to get the bloodwork done. I mention that because we took the pasta leftovers to a family dinner last night and the reaction was literally gasp-worthy. So that’s cool! It’s also disappointing because that recipe was really just 1:1 + eggs + a bit of oil + a significant amount of swearing to get the first roll-out to happen without shredding, and if that’s kicking the pants out of the commercial gluten-free pasta they’re used to… that’s embarrassing for the commercial GF pasta industry!

I think one of my philosophies going into it though is that I’m not going to try to… I’m not sure the best way to put it… I’m not trying to make clones of gluten foods, I’m trying to figure out gluten-free recipes that are spiritually similar but delicious in their own right, if that makes sense? The pasta was a bit of an exception, the only real difference between it and the pasta I used to make with, say, semolina, was that the colour was a little different and I couldn’t roll it as thin as I usually would (it would just tear if it got too thin).

For the bread I’m hoping that cornmeal, buckwheat, and/or almond flour can help bring interestingness to it that we’re almost certainly going to lose in the crumb… but who knows, maybe the right combination of psyllium, xanthan gum, or maybe… agar or something can help with the light fluffy crumb that I love without having it turn grainy and fragile.

Am also on the hunt for specialty malts like malted millet, malted rice, and malted buckwheat to try to do the same thing with beer (plus maybe some amylase extract to get the starch->sugar conversion rolling). I don’t expect it to be the same as, and I’m not trying to mimic, malted-barley-based beer but rather figure out a malted-then-fermented drink that’s an amazing drink, not an “amazing gluten-free beer”. Talking about that got people pretty excited around the table last night; they’ve mostly landed on wine, mead, and cider, which are all great drinks but not really “you can have a couple of these throughout the day at the lake” kind of drinks :)
